children.translated_text: Therein, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>) — [that is,] devoid of the appearance of that which is fit for association with verbal designation (<s>abhilāpasaṃsarga</s>), and free from the erroneous cognition that is opposed to [the object's] causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). [2]

body.text: ālocanājñānaṃ nirvikalpakam, tataḥ paraṃ jātyādiyojanātmakaṃ savikalpakam.[3]
body.translated_text: Apprehending cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>); what follows thereafter, consisting of the connection with universals (<s>jāti</s>) and so on, is conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>). [3]
That which is inexpressible (<s>avyapadeśya</s>) is non-conceptual; [it is] of the nature of determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>). [4] Moreover,

body.text:
"na so'sti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamād ṛte/
  anuviddham[5]iva jñānaṃ sarvaṃ śabdena bhāsate[6]//"[7]
body.translated_text:
'There is no cognition in the world that is without the accompaniment of words;
all cognition shines as if pervaded [5] by words [6].' [7]

body.text: iti[8]nyāyāt sarvam eva śabdānuviddham, iti bhāṭṭa[9]śaivavaiyākaraṇāḥ[10].
body.translated_text: By this [8] reasoning, everything is pervaded by words — thus [hold] the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> [Mīmāṃsakas], the <s>Śaivas</s>, and the grammarians [9] [10].

body.text: puruṣapravṛttyaṅgaṃ hi pramāṇam[11], tadaṅgatā ca saṃgatā tasya[12]vikalpakatvenaiva. na, arthasāmarthyena samudbhavāt.[13]tatrārthaḥ[14]pṛthivyādibhūtacatuṣṭayam. tatra pṛthvī[15]
body.translated_text: For a means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is a factor in a person's purposeful activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) [11], and its being such a factor is compatible only with its being conceptual. [Reply:] No, because [perception] arises from the power of the object itself [13]. Therein, the object [14] — earth and so on — [15]...

body.text:
Cf. PV II 3: dhīpramāṇatā pravṛttes tatpradhānatvād; PVinT97a4f.
[12]
body.translated_text:
Cf. PV II 3: <s>dhīpramāṇatā pravṛttes tatpradhānatvāt</s>; PVinT 97a4f.
[12]

body.text: mahāsanniveśavatī mṛd[16]rūparasagandhakaṭhinasparśādisvabhāvā, tatpradeśaviṣayasamudbhūtāś ca pāṣāṇaśoṇamaṇiveṇuvīraṇaprabhṛtayaḥ. evam āpaḥ[17]
body.translated_text: [Earth,] possessing vast extent, having the nature of form, taste, smell, and hard touch, etc.; and produced in particular locations of it are stones, red gems, bamboo, <s>vīraṇa</s> grass, and so on. Likewise, water [17]

body.text: śuklamadhuraśītadravasvabhāvāḥ sarasvatsaritsaraḥprabhṛtibhiḥ svabhāvair vivartante, kārakādikaṃ[18]ca tatkāryam. evam uṣṇeraṇasparśarūpaśabdasvabhāvo vahnyādiko[19][20]'pi.
body.translated_text: — having the nature of white, sweet, cold, and liquid — manifests with its own natures through rivers, streams, lakes, and so forth; and earthenware vessels (<s>kāraka</s>) and the like are its products. Likewise, fire — having the nature of hot, agitating touch, form, and sound...

The cognition of the form of stones and so on, produced by that [earth] as its object-condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>) [21], being of a restricted appearance [22], is unfit for association with words.

children.translated_text: The connection of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), the property, designation, and causal efficacy
[23] — [is perception] that which is fit [24] for this and [thus] prompts [activity]? If so,

body.text:
taddṛṣṭāv eva dṛṣṭeṣu saṃvitsāmarthyabhāvinaḥ[25]/
  smaraṇād abhilāṣeṇa vyavahāraḥ pravartate//[26]
body.translated_text:
'When those very things have been seen in the seeing of that [object],
by the power of cognition, through recollection, and with desire,
practical activity proceeds.' [25] [26]

body.text: na vikalpakam[27]apy adhyakṣam[28]. svalpakālāvasthitatvena nirodhanād[29] ūrdhvasvabalotpannavyavahāro smārtavikalpam[30]apekṣate. tad evam tadutpannam.
body.translated_text: Even conceptual [cognition] is not direct perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) [27] [28]. Because [perception] exists for only a brief moment and ceases [29], the practical activity arising from its own power thereafter depends on recollective conceptualization (<s>smārtavikalpa</s>) [30]. Thus, the practical activity arisen from that...

body.text: nirvikalpake'py astu vyavahārakam. tataś ca jñānair eva parasparam ālocy eva vyavahāryavyahārakair upadarśakopadarśyamānavyavasthā yādṛśī sthāpitā, kevalam anuvadāmas tādṛśīm aparavyutpattaye.
body.translated_text: Even in the non-conceptual [perception], let there be practical activity. And thus, by cognitions mutually examining one another, the arrangement of the conventional usage — in which the indicator and the indicated are established — whatever form it takes, it is...

body.text: tasmiṃś ca vikalpe'vidyānubhavavāsanopanīte[31][32]dravyam, tadāśritāś ca jātyādayo 'vidyābalena kalpitāḥ. kutaś cid anubhavasambandhāś ca saṃsthānopādhipāṣāṇarūparasādisvabhāvā[33]vibhāvyante. dravyādāv upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptānupalabdhatvena bādhanād avidyātvam. upalambhasambhāvitatvāc[34] ca rūpāder arthakatvam[35][36], tato dravyāder apūrvārthatve'py anarthatvād aprāmāṇyam. rūpādau gṛhītagrahaṇāt smārtatvam.[37] na cāprasiddhaviśeṣyādikaṃ[38]durmativispanditam.
body.translated_text: And in that conceptualization, which is brought about by the latent impressions of the experience of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) [31] [32], [there appears] a substance (<s>dravya</s>), and the universals (<s>jāti</s>) and so on that depend upon it are constructed by the power of ignorance. And the impressions of form [33], connected with experience from some [past cognition]...

body.text:
arthakaṃtvaṃ.
[36] Cf. PVSV ad PV I 215; PV III 6.
[37] Cf. HB* 2, 20-3,16.
[38]
body.translated_text:
<s>arthakaṃtvaṃ</s>.
[36] Cf. PVSV ad PV I 215; PV III 6.
[37] Cf. HB* 2, 20-3, 16.
[38]
For when [one's cognition] depends on seeing similarity and so on, then what is thus perceived [is mistaken] like [the perception of] silver in a shell. [39]
But there is also this: that [cognition] which arises from an internal disturbance [41] —

children.translated_text: not depending on seeing similarity and so on, like <s>timira</s> (eye-disease) and so on [43]. [44]

body.translated_text:
born from a defect [42], by nature it has a false appearance;
without depending on seeing similarity and so on, like [the perception caused by] an eye-disease (<s>timira</s>) and so on [43]. [44]

body.text:
-di sauṣirā-.

body.translated_text:
<s>-di sauṣirā-</s>.
[44] = PV III 361cd-362 = PVin I 53cd-54. Cf. PVSV 50, 17f.

body.text:
ekaṃ dharmiṇam uddiśya nānādharmasamāśrayam/
  vidhāv ekasya tadbhājam ivānyeṣām[45]upekṣakam//
body.translated_text:
'Targeting a single property-bearer, relying on various properties,
in [the case of] positive [determination], as if that [one property-bearer] shares [only that property], ignoring others; [45]

children.translated_text: [second verse:] 'It constructs practical activity whose object is unreal.'

body.translated_text:
in negation, [cognition] is distinct from that, and depends on the others;
thus the mind constructs practical activity whose object is unreal.' [first verse]

'Those [conceptualizations], having arrived at [an object] whose substrate is the division of the non-conceptualized object, [46]
do not obstruct the worldly [object] that has arisen from beginningless latent impressions.' [47]

body.text:
-vikalpārtha" bhe-.

body.text: yady ayam avidyāvirbhūtadravyādivivarto vikalpaḥ, katham akhilajantusantānasambhavī, kathañ ca mahadbhir api śāstrakṛdbhir anuvartitaḥ, kathañ ca bhavatām api pratipadyāpy avidyātvaṃ tathaiva dravyādivyavahārābhiniveśaḥ. niyatasvalakṣaṇapratibhāsajanitatvāt sarvasantānasambhavī, svalakṣaṇasyaiva dravyāditvena pratyākalanāt. tatprāptau tadarthakriyāpratilambhe samāptatvād abhilāṣasya[48]bādhakānavadhānam.
body.translated_text: If this conceptualization is a transformation [projected by] the substance and so on that has appeared through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), how does it arise in the mental continuum of all beings? How has it been followed even by great treatise-authors? And how does it [produce valid cognition]...
Even by the treatise-authors, the very arrangement of conceptual cognition has been established in that way, by those who desire happiness [49] —
'In conceptual practical activities, the fool and the wise person are equal.' [50]

body.text: Cf. Tattvopaplavasiṃha (E. Franco, "Perception, Knowledge and Disbelief", Stuttgart, 1987), p. 68, 7: "lokavyavahāraṃ prati sādṛśau bālapaṇḍitau"; Traikālyaparīkṣā (Dignāga), v. 4 (= VP III-3-55) cd: jñānaṃ praty abhilāsaṃ ca sādṛśaṃ bālapaṇḍitau".
body.translated_text: Cf. Tattvopaplavasiṃha (E. Franco, 'Perception, Knowledge and Disbelief', Stuttgart, 1987), p. 68, 7: '<s>lokavyavahāraṃ prati sādṛśau bālapaṇḍitau</s>'...

body.text: kevalaṃ bādhitatvavyavasāyāt paṇḍitas taditaro bālaḥ. mokṣākāṅkṣayā pratikṣaṇakṣīṇatām abhilakṣya "pratyakṣasya parīkṣitaṃ sākṣātkaraṇaṃ[51]dravyādikaṃ prati nāstī"ty ākhyātam.
body.translated_text: Only through the determination that [conceptualization] is sublated (<s>bādhita</s>) is one wise; the other is the fool. With the desire for liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), having observed the momentary destruction, 'the examined direct apprehension [51] of perception regarding substance and so on...'

children.text: nyāviparītasvabhāvopasaṃhārasambhavāt. śāstraṃ [52] hi mohanivartanam[53]ārabdham. sthūlaparāmarśād[54]vyāmohaḥ, sa ca sūkṣmāvāntaraparāmarśād[55] apasarati.
children.translated_text: there is the possibility of subsuming [objects] under a nature that is not otherwise distorted. For a treatise [52] is undertaken for the removal of delusion [53]. Delusion arises from grasping things grossly [54]; and that [delusion] is removed through the grasping of subtle intermediate [distinctions] [55]...

body.translated_text: Even for the treatise-authors, in regard to [worldly] objects, herein

body.text:
ḥ.
[53] Cf. TR 11, 2: "śāstraṃ mohanivartanam"; 11, 13-14: "vyāmohāpohayarabdham eva śastram".
[54]

yathā rūpam iti cakṣurvijñānajanakatvena saṅketaḥ kṛtaḥ evaṃ svagrāhīndriyajñānāpekṣayā rasādike'pi vākyam[56]. tato ghaṭapaṭapaṅkapallavādiṣu tadanyavyāvṛttena rūpeṇa rūpādayo 'bhinnāḥ[57]vyavahriyante. vyavahārahetur ekapratyavamarśapratyayaḥ, ekasya pratyava

children.text: marśa[58]ekatvāropī[59]pratyavamarśa ity arthaḥ. sa cāpy avidyāvaśād[60] ekatvāropī. tadbalāt sāmānyaṃ kalpayanti, arūpādirūpasāmānyānupalambhāntaraparāmarśāt[61][62] tanniṣedhaḥ.
children.translated_text: unity[58] — this is the meaning. And that too superimposes unity[59] through the force of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)[60]. Through its power they construct universals (<s>sāmānya</s>); [this construction is] refuted because there is no subsequent grasping of a universal of form that is non-form etc.[61][62].

body.translated_text: Just as regarding form (<s>rūpa</s>), the convention is made through its being the generator of visual consciousness — likewise, regarding taste and so on, the statement is made with reference to the knowledge of the sense faculty that apprehends its own [object][56]. Consequently, in pots, cloths, mud, sprouts, and so on, form and the rest are spoken of[57] as non-different by means of the form that is the exclusion of what is other. The cause of conventional usage is the cognition of a single reflective judgment (<s>ekapratyavamarśa</s>), [meaning] the reflective judgment of one [thing] that superimposes

body.text:
svarūpā-.
[62] Cf. TR 38, 11: "dravyam arūpādirūpam"; NC 780, 2: "na sāmānyākhyaḥ, arūpāditvāt, khapuṣpavat".
body.translated_text:
reads: svarūpā-.
[62] Cf. TR 38, 11: "dravyam arūpādirūpam"; NC 780, 2: "na sāmānyākhyaḥ, arūpāditvāt, khapuṣpavat".

[Verse:] Those which, though different, are invariably connected — like sense faculties and so on — by their own nature, / in the accomplishment of a single purpose, such as the knowledge [whose] object is the meaning of a single reflective judgment —[63]

body.text: tadatadvibhāgo'pi tadekaparāmarśabahulena sakṛd upapadyate. ataś[64]ca vānyonyāśrayaṇam api nāśrayaṇīyam.
body.translated_text: Even the distinction of that and non-that is established at once through the predominance of the reflective judgment of that as one. And therefore[64] mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśrayaṇa</s>) too should not be relied upon.

body.text: dṛśyavikalpyāv[65]arthāv ekīkṛtya vyavahārapravṛtter[66]visaṃvādaś[67] ca. dṛśyaḥ sphuṭatvena gṛhyamāṇaḥ, pūrvatayā pratīyamāno vikalpyaḥ[68]. kaḥ punar asau, ubhayathāpi nīla evaikībhūto'rthaḥ. sa cāsphuṭo nīlo'rthakriyāvirahalakṣaṇabādhakapramāṇena.
body.translated_text: Since conventional activity operates by unifying[65] the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) and the conceptualized (<s>vikalpya</s>) objects[66], there is no contradiction[67]. The ‘seen’ is that which is apprehended as clear; the ‘conceptualized’ is that which is cognized through a prior [experience][68]. What then is that [object]? In both ways, it is the very same object unified as ‘blue.’ And that indistinct blue is [refuted] by a valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that invalidates [it], having the characteristic of exclusion from causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>).

body.text:
-vikalpāv.
[66] VR 55, 16-17; 73, 25. Cf. PVSV 39, 7-8: "te tu..... dṛśyavikalpyāv arthāv ekīkṛtya pravartante". TUS p. 92; 93: "dṛśyavikalypāv arthāv ekikṛtya tadadhyavasāyena pravartante". Cf. J 226, 24-25; R 137, 3f.
[67]

children.text: vṛttisvabhāvo'poha[69]" ity ucyate. etena svavāgvirodho'pi pratyākhyātaḥ.
children.translated_text: reality[69]’ — thus it is stated. By this, even the objection of self-contradiction in one’s own words is refuted.

body.translated_text: ‘<s>Apoha</s> (exclusion), whose nature is the exclusion of what is other, is the ultimate

body.text:
"naimittikyāḥ śruter artham arthaṃ vā pāramārthikam[70]/
  śabdānāṃ pratirundhāno na bādhyas[71]tena varṇitaḥ//"[72]
body.translated_text: [Verse:] ‘One who blocks the objects — both causal [objects] of verbal cognition and the ultimate object[70] — / of words, is described as not being invalidated by that.[71]’[72]

body.text:
.
[72] = PV IV 128 = PVin III v.28. Cf. T. Tani, "The Problem of Interpretation on Pramāṇaviniścaya III ad vv. 28-29" (The Bulletin of the Kochi National College of Technology, No. 29, 1988).

By this reasoning. Likewise, when there is the restriction of a single reflective judgment[73],
the conventional usages of expressive words, gender, relation, universals, co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), and so on[74][75] should be understood.

body.text:
vicchedaṃ sūcayann[77]ekam apratikṣipya vartate/
  yadānyaṃ tena sa vyāpta ekatvena ca bhāsate//
body.translated_text: [76]Indicating distinction, one [word] operates without rejecting[77] / another; when by that [another word] it is pervaded, it appears with oneness. //
[Verse:] There would be co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>)[78] then, conforming to the cognition.[79]

body.text: anyathā nīlotpalādiśabdānāṃ guṇajātyādibhedād anekārthatvenaikatropasaṃhārābhāvān[80]na sāmānādhikaraṇyam, nāpi viṣayatve[81]'py ekatropasaṃhāras[82]tannimittānām ekatra samavāyād iti cet, āyāsevat[83]vivartate svapakṣanirvāhanirbandhenāndham-bhaviṣṇuḥ paraḥ. param ayam anupalambho bhūyiṣṭhadauṣṭaryaniṣṭhyūtaparānurodhaḥ[84]paripanthī. tataś cādyāpoho[85] 'nyavyāvṛttir[86][87]ekapratyavamarśaviṣayo[88]dṛśyavikalpyārthaikīkṛtaḥ[89]svabhāva ity anarthāntaram. gatam ānuṣaṅgikam.
body.translated_text: Otherwise, since the words ‘blue lotus’ and the like, due to the difference of quality, class, etc., would have multiple meanings and there would be no convergence on a single [referent][80], there would be no co-reference. ‘Nor is there convergence on a single [referent] even though they have a single object[81], because their causes[82] inhere in a single [substrate]’ — if so, the opponent, blindly persisting in maintaining his own position, exerts himself fruitlessly[83]. Moreover, this non-apprehension, being the adversary [of the opponent’s view], with conformity to the other [position] spat out through the extreme of perversity[84], is an obstacle. Therefore, the primary <s>apoha</s>[85] (exclusion), [which is] the exclusion of what is other[86][87], having as its object a single reflective judgment[88], [and having] the nature of the unification of the seen and conceptualized objects[89] — this is nothing other [than what has been stated]. The incidental [discussion] is concluded.
Just as with the conventional usage of universals[90], so too the conventional usage of substances like pots and so on should be understood.

body.text: teṣām eva ghaṭādīnāṃ[91]sādhāraṇaṃ yat phalam udakāharaṇam, tatra

children.text: ye hetavo na bhavanti ghaṭasanniveśenāvasthitā rūpādayaḥ, tebhyo vyavacchede ghaṭaśrutiḥ. evaṃ ghaṭādiśrutir api vivṛtā. uktañ ca
children.translated_text: those causes which are not [the causes] — namely, form and the rest arranged in the configuration of a pot — from which the exclusion [is made], [that is] the word ‘pot.’ Thus the word ‘pot’ and the like is also explained. And it has been said:

body.translated_text: Of those very things such as pots[91], the common result is the carrying of water. Therein,
[Verse:] ‘The word “pot” operates without cancelling the distinct capacities of form and the rest, / [functioning] in the exclusion of what is not the cause of the same result[92] as that. //

body.text:
tato[93]na rūpaṃ ghaṭa ity ekādhikaraṇā śrutiḥ/
  bhedaś[94]cāyam ato jātisamudāyābhidhāyinoḥ[95]//"[96]iti.
body.translated_text: Therefore[93] the verbal cognition ‘form is a pot’ does not have a single substrate; / and this is the difference between that which expresses a class (<s>jāti</s>) and that which expresses an aggregate (<s>samudāya</s>)[94][95].’[96]

body.text:
saṃsthānavarṇāvayavair viśiṣṭe yaḥ pravartate/
  śabdo na tasyāvayave pravṛttir upalabhyate//[97]
body.translated_text: [Verse:] A word that operates with respect to [something] distinguished by configuration, color, and parts — / its application to the parts [alone] is not perceived. //[97]

Just as the wheel, the painted, the <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure), and the like[99].

children.text: nanu tantuṣu prāvaraṇādikāryaṃ sambhavi, ghaṭe[100]'sambhavi[101], tatas tat tebhyo'rthāntaraṃ ghaṭaḥ[102]. yathā -- udakadhāraṇam asambhavi paṭe ghaṭe sambhavat, paṭād ghaṭaṃ bhedena vyavasthāpayati. satyam. sidhyaty evam arthāntaram. na punaḥ kriyāvad guṇavat samavāyikāraṇaṃ[103]dravyaṃ parābhipretaṃ sidhyati. raṇḍākaraṇḍaparipiṇḍitebhyo hi tantubhyas[104]tānapratitānībhūtā anye[105]tantavaḥ śaktibhede'pi bhinnāḥ sidhyanti.
children.translated_text: Objection: In threads, the effect of being a garment and so on is possible; in a pot[100], it is not possible[101]; therefore the pot is something different from them[102]. Just as — the holding of water, not being possible in a cloth but being possible in a pot, establishes the pot as different from the cloth. True. Thus something different is indeed established. However, the substance (<s>dravya</s>) as intended by the opponent — having action, having qualities, and being the inherence-cause[103] — is not established. For from threads arranged in the configuration of a ball, a coil, and a lump[104], other[105] threads that have become warp and weft are established as different even when there is a difference in capacity.

body.text:
paṭaḥ.

body.text: na vayaṃ dravyasyopari baddhakruddhaḥ[106], kin tarhi pratyakṣam evan nakṣate[107] 'nupalabhamānaṃ dravyam arūpādirūpam[108]. tasmān naikarūpā rūpādayas tantvādayo vā, teṣām evāntaraśaktibhedād rūpatantughaṭapaṭarajjuprabhṛtayo vyapadeśāḥ[109], na tu vyapa

children.text: deśebhyo[110]'rthāntaraparikalpanam[111]ucitam. tad uktam "aparāparapratyayayogena[112]pratikṣaṇaṃ santavantaḥ[113]saṃskārā yady api kutaścit sāmyāt[114] sarūpāḥ pratīyante, tathāpi bhinna evaiṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ[115], tena kiñcid eva kasya cit kāraṇam"[116] iti.

body.translated_text: We are not angry about[106] substance as such; rather, perception itself does not perceive[107] substance, which is not apprehended, [defined as] that which is form but not form-and-the-rest[108]. Therefore, form and the rest, or threads and the like, are not of a single nature; due to the internal difference of capacities among those very [things], the designations ‘form,’ ‘thread,’ ‘pot,’ ‘cloth,’ ‘rope,’ and so forth [arise][109]. But constructing something different from the designations[110][111] is not appropriate. As it has been said: ‘Formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), which continue through the connection of successive conditions[112], moment by moment[113], although they appear to be of the same form due to some similarity[114], nevertheless their nature is indeed different[115]; therefore, only something specific is the cause of something specific.’[116]
Let the entity (<s>vastu</s>) constructed by the other as substance and so on be visible or invisible[117][118].
"The non-operation of the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) [occurs] when there is no fruit of non-operation."

body.text: iti nyāyāt[121]sad iti na vyavahartavyam. ekapratyavamarśam apekṣyāpunarupalabhyamānena[122] vyavahāraḥ.
body.translated_text: By this principle, one should not engage in the convention "it exists." The convention [operates] through that which is not apprehended again, in dependence on a single reflective cognition.

body.text: tad evam [Sh39] indriyārthād utpadyamānaṃ niyatapratibhāsam[123][124]api yatpratibhāsāc[125] cāvidyānubhavavāsanāvaśād[126][127]udīyamānaṃ jñānam.
body.translated_text: Thus, the cognition that arises from the sense object, having a determinate appearance, and which arises due to the force of the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of the experience of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) from that very appearance,
Here is the formal argument: That which does not connect the natures of earlier and later moments—

one having an appearance fit for association with words useful at the time of conventional usage based on signs, just as the experience whose object is the intrinsic nature of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) of form, etc.; and the cognition born from the eye and form, endowed with the aforementioned means of proof.

This is a cognition of a reason that contradicts the cause, which is to be considered plausible. There is no unestablished [reason].
Because it is shaken away like the wife of the Sindhu river,

body.text:
"pratibhāso'sya nāsyeti nopapattes tu gocaraḥ/" iti,
  "saṃvedanasya tādātmye na vivādo'sti kasya cit/"[137]
body.translated_text:
"The appearance of this [cognition] does not exist in it—this is not tenable; rather, it is the object," thus,
"When <s>saṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) is identical [with the cognition], there is no dispute for anyone."

body.text: iti nyāyāt. svarūpasaṃvedanād eva yathoktaniyatasvabhāvasiddheḥ. aniyatapratibhāse śabdasaṅketasya susaṅkalitatvāt[138]kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau satyāṃ na śaṃsanīyam[139] aṃśenāpi[140] saṃśayāvahatvam asya. nāpi virodho'pi nāmāsya sannidhānam anubadhnāti.
body.translated_text: By this principle: because the aforementioned determinate nature is established through <s>svarūpasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness of one's own nature) alone. When the causal relation is established through the well-coordinated nature of verbal convention in the case of indeterminate appearance, it should not be said that even partially it produces doubt. Nor does its presence entail any contradiction whatsoever.
[This] brings about the status of a positive instance, because it is possible in the experience of the intrinsic nature of <s>vikalpa-vijñāna</s> (conceptual cognition).
The position that cognition is indirect will be refuted.
How can that which has an indeterminate appearance be the cause of the application of words? It is replied—

body.text:
"viśeṣaṇaṃ[143]viśeṣyañ ca sambandhaṃ laukikīṃ sthitim/
  gṛhītvā saṅkalayyaitat tathā pratyeti nānyathā//
body.translated_text:
"Having grasped the <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier), the <s>viśeṣya</s> (qualified), the relation, and the worldly convention,
and having coordinated these, [the cognition] cognizes thus and not otherwise.
As in [the case of] one who possesses a staff."

body.text: = PV III 145-146a. Cf. PVin I v. 7.
body.translated_text: = PV III 145-146a. Cf. PVin I v. 7.

body.text: yad vijñānaṃ viśeṣaṇarūpatayā vācakaṃ paricchinatti, rūpatayā ca nīlādikam.
body.translated_text: That cognition which distinguishes the designator in the form of a <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier), and [distinguishes] blue and so forth in the form [of the qualified].
Even with a nature that pervades the time of conventional usage of relation, it could be a <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier) and a <s>viśeṣya</s> (qualified).

body.text: tādṛśañ ca rūpaṃ gṛhṇad viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ [Sh40] vā gṛhṇīyāt.
body.translated_text: And grasping such a form, it would grasp either the <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier) or the <s>viśeṣya</s> (qualified).

body.text: viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoś[146]ca sambandham. laukikīṃ sthitiṃ puruṣo daṇḍī na puruṣī daṇḍa iti.
body.translated_text: And the relation between <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier) and <s>viśeṣya</s> (qualified). The worldly convention: "The person has a staff, not the staff has a person."

body.text: śiromān[147]samagreṇa[148]śṛṅgeṇa śṛṅgī, na galake lambamānena. tathā samastaṃ smṛtvā viśeṣaṇayuktaviśeṣyaṃ sakṛd gṛhṇāti, nānevaṃrūpatve.
body.translated_text: One who has a head-ornament is "horned" by virtue of a complete horn, not by one hanging from the throat. Likewise, having recalled the whole, one grasps the <s>viśeṣya</s> (qualified) endowed with the <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier) at once, and not when it does not have such a form.

body.text: tathā hi puruṣaś cāsti daṇḍaś ca, kiṃ na sarve daṇḍinaḥ saṃyogāc cet, saṃyogo'py asti.
body.translated_text: For indeed, there is a person and there is a staff—why are not all [persons] "staff-bearers"? If [you say] because of contact, contact also exists.

body.text: kiṃ na sarve daṇḍinaḥ, saṃyogasya guṇatvena yatrāsau samavetaḥ sa eva daṇḍīti cet, samavāyo'py asti. kiṃ na sarve daṇḍinaḥ, yadaṅgatayā gṛhyate sa eva daṇḍīti cet, evaṃ tarhi daṇḍāder api[149]sāṃvṛtatām abhikhyāyāta[150].
body.translated_text: Why are not all staff-bearers? If [you say] because the one in which [contact], being a quality, inheres is the staff-bearer, <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) also exists—why are not all staff-bearers? If [you say] the one who is grasped as having it as a limb is the staff-bearer, then one should declare the conventional nature of the staff and so forth as well.

body.text: yat pūrvāparakālānanusandhāyi viśeṣaṇena saha viśeṣyasyāgrāhakañ[151]ca[152]tan niyatapratibhāsam ucyate, tat kathaṃ na kāraṇaṃ viruddham.
body.translated_text: That which does not connect the earlier and later moments, and does not grasp the <s>viśeṣya</s> (qualified) together with the <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualifier)—that is said to have a determinate appearance. How is the cause not contradicted?

Of the tree of cognition, whose self is impelled by the gust of wind of powerful <s>vikalpa-vāsanā</s> (latent impressions of conceptual cognition), the shadow of cognitive content falls in one direction while the withered leaves of <s>adhyavasāya</s> (ascertainment) drift in another.

body.text: atha ko[155]'dhyavasāyo nāma. yadi grahaṇaṃ grahaṇam iti vaktavyam, athāpi [M20a] tadabhāvas tathāpy agrahaṇam evāstu. satyam. asannihitatayānusandhānam adhyavasāyo grahaṇaviśeṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: Now, what is <s>adhyavasāya</s> (ascertainment) by name? If [it is] apprehension, then [simply] say "apprehension." Or if it is the absence of that, even so let it be non-apprehension. True. <s>Adhyavasāya</s> (ascertainment) is a particular type of apprehension that is a connecting cognition of something as not present.

body.text: yat smaraṇādisāmagrīrahitendriyajanitaṃ[156]tan nirvikalpam[157]astu, yat smaraṇādisāmagrīsavyapekśendriyajaṃ tad vikalpakam[158]astu. na,

children.translated_text: because [<s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception)] does not operate on a non-object.

body.translated_text: Let that which is produced by the senses devoid of the conditions such as memory, etc., be <s>nirvikalpa</s> (non-conceptual); let that which is produced by the senses in dependence on the conditions such as memory, etc., be <s>savikalpa</s> (conceptual). No,

body.text: pratyakṣasyāsannihitaṃ[159]viśeṣaṇatvādi na viṣayaḥ. viśeṣaṇatvaṃ hi na vastunaḥ[160]sampraty asti.
body.translated_text: The qualifier-hood and so forth, which are not present to <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), are not its object. For qualifier-hood does not presently belong to the real thing.

body.text: astitve[161]kiṃ[162]smaraṇena, tataś ca smaraṇenopanītam api viśeṣaṇatvādi nāsannihitatvaṃ[163] jahāti.
body.translated_text: If it exists [in the thing itself], what need is there for memory? And therefore, even though qualifier-hood and so forth are brought in by memory, they do not lose their character of not being present.
Therefore, because of not being present, [qualifier-hood] is not an object of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).

body.text: na ca jātyādiviśiṣṭārthavikalpaś cakṣurarthasannidhāv eva bhavati, atītādiṣv api sambhavāt, vinā cārthaiḥ nimīlitavilocanasyāpi[164]gaur iti vikalpanāt.[165]
body.translated_text: And the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) of an object qualified by universals and so forth does not occur only when the object is present to the eye, since it is possible even with regard to past objects and so forth, and because even one with closed eyes conceptualizes "a cow" without objects.

body.text: nānyathedantayeti[166]cet. idantayā viśiṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ na[167]sannihitārthaniścayarūpam adhyakṣam akṣasāpekṣañ ca, ubhayanirapekṣatvāt[168]. tathā hi "śuklo gaur ayam" iti cākṣuṣo[169] 'nantaraṃ tathā spṛśato 'pi "sukumāraḥ śuklo 'yaṃ gaur" iti. ubhayaviṣayam api niścayanam idantayā viśiṣṭam.
body.translated_text: If [the opponent says] "it is not otherwise than [qualified by] 'this-ness,'" [we reply:] A cognition qualified by this-ness is not a <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) in the form of ascertainment of a present object, nor is it dependent on the senses, because it is independent of both. For example, immediately after a visual [perception] "this is a white cow," even while touching [it], [one cognizes] "this is a soft white cow." The ascertainment qualified by this-ness has both [visual and tactile] objects.

body.text: na cāndhatamase rūpasya śaktir asti, na vā cakṣuṣaḥ. na ca sparśenendriyeṇa[170]rūpagrahaṇam evaṃ sparśasya cakṣuṣi vyabhicāro vācyaḥ. tasmāc cakṣuḥsparśanābhyāṃ[171]bhinnaṃ viṣayam upalabhyānyad eva tatsahacarasamudāyaviṣayaṃ smārtam[172]abhedajñānam utpadyate.[173][174] tathā viśeṣyān svair indriyair bhinnān upalabhyārthāntaravya[M20b]vacchedaviṣayam[175]abhedena[176] sarvatra mānasaṃ jñānam utpadyate. na bhāvaguṇatvayoḥ pratyakṣam, tasyānupalakṣaṇāt[177].
body.translated_text: And in complete darkness, form has no capacity [to be perceived], nor does the eye. And there is no apprehension of form by the sense of touch; likewise, the deviation of touch with respect to the eye should be stated. Therefore, having perceived different objects through the eye and the sense of touch, a different <s>smārta</s> (memory-based) cognition of non-difference arises, having as its object the aggregate of those concomitants. Similarly, having perceived the qualified [objects] as different through their respective senses, a mental cognition of non-difference arises everywhere, having as its object the exclusion of other things. The universal and quality-hood are not [objects of] <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), because they are not observed [by it].

body.text: uktañ ca [Sh42] "darśanasparśanānvayo[179]mānasa eva smārto[180]vibhrama" iti. "yam aham adrakṣaṃ tam eva[181]hi spṛśāmī"ti[182]vikalpād[183]dravyaparikalpaḥ kalpāvadhivyasanam, bhrāntyaiva samarthitatvāt. tasmān mano 'bhisaṃskṛtam arthaviśeṣaṇam arthaṃ nendriyaṃ pratyeti.
body.translated_text: And it has been said: "The correlation of seeing and touching is indeed a mental, memory-based <s>vibhrama</s> (error)." From the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) that "I now touch the very same thing that I saw," arises the construction of a substance (<s>dravyaparikalpana</s>), which is the fault of superimposition (<s>kalpāvadhivyasana</s>), since it is established only through error. Therefore, what is mentally constructed as a qualifier of the object (<s>arthaviśeṣaṇa</s>) — the sense faculty does not perceive that object.

body.text: yat pratyekaṃ samudāye ca tad vastuno rūpam[184], tad yathā nīlatvam. yat pratyekam asat samudāye cāsti sa samudāyadharmaḥ, yathā caturasratvādi.[185]sthaulyaṃ tu samudāyapratibhāsadharmaḥ[186].[187]bahuṣu pratibhāsamāneṣu nirantareṣu sthūlam iti pratyayaḥ. tena rūpaṃ sparśo vā sthūlaḥ, na tu tadatiriktaṃ dravyaṃ sthūlam apatibhāsanāt.
body.translated_text: That which exists in each individual and also in the aggregate is the real nature (<s>rūpa</s>) of the object — for example, blueness (<s>nīlatva</s>). That which does not exist in each individual but exists in the aggregate is a property of the aggregate (<s>samudāyadharma</s>), such as squareness (<s>caturaśratva</s>) and the like. Grossness (<s>sthaulya</s>), however, is a property of the appearance of the aggregate (<s>samudāyapratibhāsadharma</s>). When many [atoms] appear without gaps between them, there arises the cognition "this is gross." Therefore, it is color (<s>rūpa</s>) or touch (<s>sparśa</s>) that is gross, but not any substance (<s>dravya</s>) beyond them, since such a substance does not appear.

body.text:

-prati..bhāsa-.

M [reads] -prati..bhāsa-.

body.text: atha yadi pratibhāsadharmaḥ sthaulyaṃ tadā tat kim āntaram āhosvid bahiḥ, atha tad antar na[188]na bahir yad eva ca punar nistattvam[189]āropitam iti cet. tadāpi nāsty eveti vaktavyam. kim ucyate, "pratibhāsadharmaḥ sthaulyam" iti. satyam, sthaulyaṃ nāmāsthūlaparāvṛttaṃ rūpam, na vidhirūpaṃ kiñ cit. tato nistattvam[190]api sthūlaparāmarśena[191]vyavahriyamāṇatvāt saṃvṛtisad etan, na tu nāsty eva sarvathā. sāmānyam evaikapratyavamarśaviṣayatvena yathāsti. āha ca --
body.translated_text: Now, if grossness (<s>sthaulya</s>) is a property of appearance (<s>pratibhāsadharma</s>), then is it internal or external? If it is neither internal nor external, and moreover is something unreal (<s>nistattva</s>) that is superimposed — even so, it must be said that it simply does not exist. Why then is it said, "grossness is a property of appearance"? True, grossness is merely a form that is the exclusion of the non-gross (<s>asthūlaparāvṛtta rūpa</s>); it is not any positive entity (<s>vidhirūpa</s>). Therefore, even though it is unreal, since it is dealt with through the apprehension of grossness, it is conventionally real (<s>saṃvṛtisat</s>) — but it does not absolutely not exist in every respect. <s>Sāmānya</s> (universality) exists just as it is, as the object of a single reflective cognition (<s>ekapratyavamarśa</s>). And he says —

children.translated_text: through being the cause of the cognition of grossness, the grossness of things (<s>bhāvas</s>) is acknowledged."

body.translated_text: "Because [grossness] is the cause of the reflective cognition of grossness (<s>sthūlapratyavamarśa</s>), it is the grossness of cognition;

venabhā.

M repeats venabhā.
[193] Cf. PV I 109: "ekapratyavamarśasya hetutvād dhir abhedinī/ ekadhīhetubhāvena vyaktīnām apy abhinnatā//"
Objection: Does <s>pratyavamarśa</s> (reflective cognition) alone superimpose grossness?

body.text: pratyavamarśa eva kiṃ sthūlam āropayatīti cet.

"astīyam api yā tv antarupaplavasamudbhavā/
  doṣodbhavā prakṛtyā sā vitathapratibhāsinī//"[194]
body.translated_text:
"Even this [cognition] which exists, but which arises from internal disturbance,
born from defects (<s>doṣa</s>), is by its nature one that presents false appearances."

body.text: iti nyāyād avidyānubhavavāsanābhāvitvād ity asakṛd uktam.[195][196]tena sthūlaṃ nīlam iti pratibhāse 'pi na[197]nīle vasturūpe vibhramaḥ. vibhramas tu śaṅkhe pītapratibhāsaḥ. śuklaṃ[198]hi rūpaṃ pratyekaṃ samudāye[199]cāsti vastuno rūpam.[200]tatsamudāyadharmaś ca saṃsthānam.
body.translated_text: By the reasoning that [such cognition] has the nature of a <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) born from the experience of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), this has been stated repeatedly. Therefore, even in the appearance of "gross" and "blue," there is no error (<s>vibhrama</s>) regarding the real nature (<s>vasturūpa</s>) of blue. Error, however, is the appearance of yellow in a conch shell. For white color (<s>śukla rūpa</s>) exists both in each individual [atom] and in the aggregate — it is the real nature of the object. And the property of that aggregate is configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>).

body.text:
samudaye.
[200] Cf. TR 42, 5: "yat pratyekaṃ samudāye ca tad vastuno rūpam".
body.translated_text:
Sh [reads] samudaye.
[200] Cf. TR 42, 5: "yat pratyekaṃ samudāye ca tad vastuno rūpam".

body.text: śuklāpratibhāse tadātmakasaṃstānasyāpratibhāsaḥ. tataḥ pītaśaṅkhajñānaṃ nāṅgenāpi saṃvādakam, nāpi ca vastunaḥ sākṣātkārakam. ato viśeṣaṇadvayaṃ vipratipattinirākaraṇārtham.
body.translated_text: When white does not appear, the configuration having that nature also does not appear. Therefore, the cognition of a yellow conch shell does not accord (<s>saṃvāda</s>) even partially, nor does it directly perceive (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) the object. Hence, the two qualifications (<s>viśeṣaṇadvaya</s>) [in the definition of perception] are for the purpose of removing disagreement (<s>vipratipattinirākaraṇa</s>).

body.text: yat punar bhrāntijñāne[201], "alaukikatvād ubhayātmayogāt smṛtipramoṣād viparītacittair[202]" ityādinānāvyavahṛtiḥ. tatra na nāmni vivadāmahe. vivakṣitavasturūpaṃ na sākṣātkṛtam iti tu paramārthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Now, regarding erroneous cognition (<s>bhrāntijñāna</s>), there are various designations such as "because it is non-worldly (<s>alaukika</s>), because it has the nature of both, because of the loss of memory (<s>smṛtipramoṣa</s>), [and because it is held] by those with inverted minds (<s>viparītacitta</s>)." In this matter, we do not dispute about names. The essential point (<s>paramārtha</s>) is that the intended real nature of the object has not been directly perceived.
"Therefore, cognition [arising] from the object is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception)" — this definition by the venerable master <s>Vasubandhu</s> is deficient.

body.text: naiyāyikīyam "indriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyātmakaṃ pratyakṣam". vaiśeṣikīyam "dravyeṣu pratyakṣam ātmendriyamano 'rthasannikarṣād yan niṣpadyate tad anyad" iti.

children.text: kāpilānām api "śrotrādivṛttiḥ pratyakṣam. śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇānāṃ[203]manasādhiṣṭhitā[204]vṛttiḥ [M21b] śabdasparśarūparasagandheṣu yathākramaṃ grahaṇe vartamānā pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam".
children.translated_text: According to the <s>Kāpilas</s> (Sāṃkhyas) as well: "The activity (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the ear and other [sense organs] is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception). The activity of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose — governed by <s>manas</s> (mind) — operating in the apprehension of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell respectively, is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) called <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception)."

body.translated_text: The <s>Naiyāyika</s> [definition]: "Cognition born from the contact of sense organ and object, which is non-verbal (<s>avyapadeśya</s>), non-errant (<s>avyabhicārin</s>), and of the nature of determination (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>), is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception)." The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> [definition]: "Regarding substances (<s>dravya</s>), <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) is that which arises from the contact of self (<s>ātman</s>), sense organ (<s>indriya</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and object — it is distinct [from other forms of knowledge]."

body.text: mīmāmsāyām "satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣam". sarvam etad dravyaguṇātmādinirākaraṇād[205]ayathārtham.
body.translated_text: In <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>: "The cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) born in a person from the actual contact (<s>satsaṃprayoga</s>) of the sense organs is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception)." All these [definitions] are inaccurate (<s>ayathārtha</s>), because they fail to exclude [the cognition of] substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), self (<s>ātman</s>), and the like.

children.translated_text: Thus concludes the second [chapter], the determination of the principles regarding the definition of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣalakṣaṇa</s>) of one's own and others' [systems], in the <s>Tarkarahasya</s>.
